chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it, said:

When Dharr ibn Abu Zarr died, Abu Zarr wiped the grave with his hand, then said: 'May Allah have mercy on you, O Dharr! By Allah, you were righteous with me, and you have died and I am pleased with you. However, by Allah, I am not disappointed due to your death and I do not have any sadness or grief, and I have no need for anyone besides Allah. Had it not been for the fear of the One who inspects (the Hereafter), I would have been happy to be in your place. My sadness for you (concern for your state in the Hereafter) has kept me from sadness due to your death. By Allah, I did not weep because of your death, but I wept for you (for what you may face). I do not know what I said about you and what is said about you.'

Then he said: 'O Allah, I have gifted to him whatever You necessitated upon him from my rights, therefore gift to him whatever You necessitated upon him from Your Rights, for You are more rightful with Benevolence than I am.'

key_terms.الْحُزْنُ عَلَيْكَ: Sadness over you (grief for your death)
key_terms.الْحُزْنُ لَكَ: Sadness for you (concern for your state in the afterlife)
key_terms.الْمُطَّلَعِ: The One who inspects (Allah), referring to the fear of the Hereafter
key_terms.حَقِّكَ: Your right (due to you from Allah)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Abu Zarr weeping for his son rather than over his death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the profound spiritual bond between father and son, highlighting Abu Zarr’s unique state of 'contentment' (rida) despite the natural sorrow of loss. The narrative emphasizes the concept of transferring personal rights (haqq al-adam) to the deceased, a practice reflecting the Shia understanding of intercession and divine generosity, where the father’s petition for Dharr’s standing in the Hereafter underscores the belief that the righteous continue to benefit from the piety of their loved ones.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, raising it, said,

‘When Zharr son of Abu Zarr<sup>as</sup> died, Abu Zarr<sup>as</sup> wiped the grave with his<sup>as</sup> hand, then said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you, O Zharr! By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You were righteous with me<sup>as</sup>, and you have died and I<sup>as</sup> am pleased with you.  However, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I am not disappointed due to your death and I do not need anyone beside Allah<sup>azwj</sup>.  Had it not been for fear from the next life I would have been happy to be in your place.  My sadness for you (my concern for you in the next life) has kept me from sadness due to your death.  By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I do not weep because of your death but I weep for you because of what you may face in the next life.  I do not know what I have said about you and what is said about you.

Then he<sup>ra</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I<sup>ra</sup> have gifted to him whatever was necessitated upon him from my rights, therefore Gift to him whatever was necessitated upon him from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Rights, for You<sup>azwj</sup> are more rightful with the Benevolence than I<sup>as</sup> am’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated in a marfu‘ manner the following: “

When Dharr, son of abu Dharr passed away, abu Dharr wiped his grave with his hand and said, ‘May Allah grant you mercy, O Dharr, by Allah, you were kind to me and I am satisfied with you. By Allah, I am not disappointed due to your death and I do not need anyone beside Allah. Had it not been for fear from the next life I would have been happy to be in your place. My sadness for you (my concern about your condition in the next life) has kept me from sadness due to your death. By Allah, I do not weep because of your death but I weep for you because of what you may face in the next life. I do not know what I have said about you and what is said about you.’
Then he said, ‘O Lord, I have waived in his favor my rights that You had set on him. Please waive in his favor Your rights on him; You are more generous than I.’”
